sections.title: Article heading
sections.text:
ARTICLE 553.

PD 553.

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 553 was established by Ordinance No. 23929, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 23, 1999. Ordinance No. 23929 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 23929; 25163)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 553 is established on property generally located on the east line of Preston Road, at its intersection with the south line of Orchid Lane. The size of PD 553 is approximately 40.4926 acres. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this article:

(1) HEADMASTER’S DWELLING UNIT means a residential dwelling for a school executive.

(2) NATATORIUM means a building which contains an indoor pool.

(3) OVERFLOW PARKING means off-street parking for any event which occurs on the Property after 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, or on weekends, during any academic school year.

(4) SPECIAL EVENT means an activity that is not a part of the routine school day and that involves an increase in traffic to the Property which cannot be reasonably accommodated by the Preston Road entrances. Special events may include certain sports events and weekend activities.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 31893)

SEC. 51P-553.103.1. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 553A: Subarea A development/screening plan.

(2) Exhibit 553B: conceptual plan.

(3) Exhibit 553C: traffic management plan. (Ord. Nos. 28290; 30170; 31893)

SEC. 51P-553.103.2. CREATION OF SUBAREAS.

This district is divided into two subareas, Subarea A and Subarea B as shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit 553B). (Ord. 31893)

SEC. 51P-553.103.3. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31893)

sections.title: Development/Screening Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.104. DEVELOPMENT/SCREENING PLAN.

(a) Subarea A. Except as provided in this section, development and use of the Property must comply with the Subarea A development/screening plan (Exhibit 553A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the Subarea A development/screening plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) Subarea B. A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(c) Future paved parking area. No structures are permitted in the “future paved parking” area shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan except for a headmaster’s dwelling unit. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

-- Church. -- Private school for grades K through 12. -- Headmaster’s dwelling unit. [Only in the future paved parking area shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.] -- Natatorium. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.106. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations contained in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Headmaster’s dwelling unit.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-16(A) Single Family District apply.

(2) The maximum number of dwelling units is one.

(b) All other uses.

(1) Front, side, and rear yard. Minimum front, side, and rear yards are as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(2) Density. No maximum dwelling unit density.

(3) Floor area. Maximum floor area ratio is as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(4) Height.

(A) In general. Except as provided in Subparagraphs (B), (C), and (D) below, maximum structure heights are as follows:

(i) Subarea A.

(aa) Building B – 38 feet.

(bb) Building C – 38 feet.

(cc) Building D – 24 feet.

(dd) Building E – 41 feet.

(ee) Building F – 38 feet.

(ff) Building G – 38 feet.

(gg) Building H – 42 feet.

(hh) Building I – 45 feet.

(ii) Athletic field netting – 40 feet.

(jj) Bell tower – 65 feet.

(kk) Chapel – 45 feet.

(ll) East stadium – 26 feet.

(mm) Flag poles – 50 feet.

(nn) Gate building – 17 feet.

(oo) Planetarium dome – 50 feet.

(ii) Subarea B. Maximum structure height is 40 feet.

(iii) Residential proximity slope. For any new structures constructed in Subarea A or Subarea B after June 9, 2021, if any portion of such structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope as defined in Section 51A-4.412.

(B) Roof-top structures. The following structures located on top of a building are allowed to project up to 12 feet above the maximum structure height:

(i) Mechanical equipment rooms.

(ii) Elevator penthouses or bulkheads.

(iii) Visual screens surrounding roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(C) Parapet walls. Parapet walls may project up to four feet above the maximum structure height.

(D) Outdoor lighting heights. Maximum heights for exterior lighting are as follows:

(i) Bollards – 42 inches.

(ii) Poles – 38 feet.

(iii) Walkway lighting – 15 feet.

(iv) Wall mounted lighting – 30 feet.

(v) Stadium lighting – 80 feet.

(5) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(6) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(7) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.108. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Off-street parking and loading must be located as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(b) Except as provided in this subsection, a minimum of 428 off-street parking spaces must be provided on the Property at all times. During construction, a minimum of 341 off-street parking spaces must be provided on the Property.

(c) Overflow parking for special events must be provided on the Property.

(d) Except as provided in this subsection, parking during school hours is prohibited in areas designated for overflow parking on the Subarea A development/screening plan. Overflow parking may be provided in the areas designated as overflow parking during school hours up to 10 times during a school year.

(e) The area identified on the Subarea A development/screening plan as “future paved parking” may not be used for parking until the earthen berm required by Section 51P-553.111(g) has been constructed.

(f) For purposes of this section, the Property is considered one lot. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.109. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.110. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Landscaping and tree mitigation must be provided as specified in this section and as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(c) Landscaping within 60 feet of Orchid Lane must be completed within 15 months of the date of issuance of a building permit for new construction on the Property. All other

landscaping must be completed within 36 months of the date of issuance of a building permit for new construction on the Property.

(d) The minimum caliper inches per tree must be three inches at the time of planting.

(e) Except as noted on the Subarea A development/screening plan, the species of all proposed canopy trees must comply with the list of approved replacement trees in Section 51A- 10.134.

(f) For purposes of this section, screening, which consists of landscape materials, fences, and berms as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan, is not considered landscaping.

(g) Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Screening And Fences
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.111. SCREENING AND FENCES.

(a) Screening on the Property must be provided in accordance with the Subarea A development/screening plan.

(b) Screening on the eastern and southwestern boundary of the Property, as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan, must consist of evergreen plant materials recommended for local area use by the director of park and recreation, and must be capable of obtaining a minimum height of four feet in three growing seasons.

(c) An orchid screening zone must be provided along the frontage of Orchid Lane and must be within the area of the 25 foot setback from the property line. This zone must be completed by June 9, 2022 and must provide the following:

(1) A minimum of 49 red oak or live oak trees with a minimum caliper of six inches planted 24 feet on center within the first 15 feet of the orchid screening zone;

(2) A column and ornamental fence with a maximum height of four-and-a-half feet and located a minimum of 25 feet from the property line; and

(3) A screening line of at least 220 oak leaf hollies planted six feet on center located along the inside of the fence.

(d) All screening must be completed within 15 months of the date of issuance of a building permit for new construction on the Property.

(e) The athletic field netting shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan along Preston Road cannot be extended along Orchid Lane. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893; 32155)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.112. SIGNS.

Except as further restricted in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for nonbusiness zoning districts in Article VII. Detached signs are only permitted along the Preston Road frontage. Flags displayed on the flag poles shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan are not included in the calculation of the maximum number of signs allowed under the provisions for nonbusiness zoning districts. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Traffic Management Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.113. TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN.

(a) In general. Operation of a private school must comply with the traffic management plan (Exhibit 553C).

(b) Queuing. Queuing is only permitted inside the Property. Student drop-off and pick-up are not permitted within city rights-of-way.

(c) Traffic study.

(1) The Property owner or operator shall prepare a traffic study evaluating the sufficiency of the traffic management plan. The initial traffic study must be submitted to the director by November 15, 2018. After the initial traffic study, the Property owner or operator shall submit updates of the traffic study to the director by November 15 of each even-numbered year.

(2) The traffic study must be in writing, performed by a licensed engineer, based on a minimum of four samples taken on different school days at different drop-off and pick- up times over a two-week period, and must contain an analysis of the following:

(A) ingress and egress points;

(B) queue lengths;

(C) number and location of personnel assisting with loading and unloading of students;

(D) drop-off and pick-up locations;

(E) drop-off and pick-up hours for each grade level;

(F) hours for each grade level; and

(G) circulation.

(3) Within 30 days after submission of a traffic study, the director shall determine if the current traffic management plan is sufficient.

(A) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan is sufficient, the director shall notify the applicant in writing.

(B) If the director determines that the current traffic management plan results in traffic hazards or traffic congestion, the director shall require the Property owner to submit an amended traffic management plan. If the Property owner fails to submit an amended traffic management plan within 30 days, the director shall notify the city plan commission.

(d) Amendment process.

(1) A traffic management plan may be amended using minor plan amendment fee and public hearing process in Section 51A-1.105(k)(3) of Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code.

(2) The city plan commission shall authorize changes in a traffic management plan if the proposed amendments improve queuing or traffic circulation; eliminate traffic hazards; or decrease traffic congestion. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Traffic Reduction
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.114. TRAFFIC REDUCTION.

(a) Generally. Traffic reduction management must be vigorously pursued.

(b) Orchid Lane access. A gate must be provided at the Orchid Lane entry which is equipped with a moveable arm that allows access to the Property only in a controlled manner. This gate must remain closed at all times other than the 7:00 - 9:30 a.m. and 2:00 - 7:00 p.m. peak hours and during special events. The gate must remain open continuously for unrestricted access to the Property during the 7:00 - 9:30 a.m. and 2:00 - 7:00 p.m. peak hours and for special events. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290)

sections.title: Preston Road
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.115. PRESTON ROAD.

(a) Preston Road Entrance No. 1. Any gate located at this entrance must automatically open and allow the free-flow of vehicles into the Property during the hours of 6:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. In the event of power failure, the gate must remain open. The gate at this entrance must be located at least 100 feet from the Property line to provide adequate stacking and turn around space.

(b) Preston Road Entrance No. 2. Preston Road Entrance No. 2 must be located and constructed as shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan and must be no less than 24 feet wide at its intersection with Preston Road. The curb radius must be no less than 20 feet. The gate at this entrance must remain continuously open between the hours of 6:00 a. m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Ingress/Egress
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.117. INGRESS/EGRESS.

All points of ingress and egress from the Property must be approved by the director of public works and transportation as to location, design, and construction. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290)

sections.title: Construction, Delivery, And Service Vehicles
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.118. CONSTRUCTION, DELIVERY, AND SERVICE VEHICLES.

(a) Except as otherwise provided in this section, construction vehicles must use the Preston Road entrances for access to the Property. Construction vehicles may use entrances other than the Preston Road entrances only when access to the construction site is significantly restricted from Preston Road or in order to allow the construction or installation of landscaping, screening, tennis courts, and parking lots around the perimeter of the Property.

(b) Upon completion of Preston Road Entrance No. 1, the owner shall require delivery vehicles, service vehicles, and busses to use Preston Road exclusively for ingress to and egress from the Property. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 28290)

sections.title: Reimbursement
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.119. REIMBURSEMENT.

The applicant shall reimburse the department of public works and transportation for the installation of traffic control signs and markings on streets contiguous to the Property necessitated by development of the Property. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163)

sections.title: Paving
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.120. PAVING.

Except as provided in this section, all parking spaces, aisles, maneuvering areas, and driveway connections to streets or alleys, whether enclosed or unenclosed, must be surfaced to comply with the requirements of Chapter 51A. The paving of areas designated as “overflow parking” on the Subarea A development/screening plan is not required. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Outdoor Lighting
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.121. OUTDOOR LIGHTING.

Outdoor lighting of all tennis courts and the playing fields near the intersection of Orchid Lane and Preston Road is prohibited. All outdoor lighting, where permitted, must be hooded and directed downward and away from adjacent properties. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 31893)

sections.title: Temporary Buildings
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.122. TEMPORARY BUILDINGS.

Buildings to be used as temporary administrative offices, contractor’s offices, bathroom facilities, classrooms, laboratories, and studios may be located outside the designated buildable areas, as those areas are shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan, for a period not to exceed 30 months from the issuance of a building permit on the Property. Nonconforming structures located within this district may be used as temporary administrative offices, contractor’s offices, classrooms, laboratories, and studios, as long as these structures are only used in this capacity for a period not to exceed 30 months from the issuance of a building permit on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Playing Fields
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.123. PLAYING FIELDS.

The playing fields located nearest the intersection of Preston Road and Orchid Lane must remain open and unobstructed, except for the perimeter fence and screening shown on the Subarea A development/screening plan. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 30170; 31893)

sections.title: Private License And Right-Of-Way Landscape
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.124. PRIVATE LICENSE AND RIGHT-OF-WAY LANDSCAPE PERMIT.

(a) The city council hereby grants a private license to the owners of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing compliance with the parkway landscaping requirements of this article. A property owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license, although a fee may be charged for issuance of a landscape permit in accordance with the Dallas Building Code. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council retains the right to terminate this license whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-of-way or whenever the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance.

(b) It is the responsibility of the property owner to apply for and obtain the required right-of-way landscape permit before locating plant materials in the right-of-way. An application for a right-of-way landscape permit must be made to the director of public works and transportation before any plant materials are located in the right-of-way. The application must be in writing on a form approved by the director and accompanied by plans or drawings showing the area of the right-of-way affected and the construction and planting proposed.

(c) Upon receipt of the application and any required fees, the director shall circulate it to all affected city departments and utilities for review and comment. If, after receiving comments from affected city departments and utilities, the director determines that the construction and planting proposed will not be inconsistent with and will not unreasonably impair the public use of the right-of-way, the director shall issue a right-of-way landscape permit; otherwise, the director shall deny the permit.
(d) A right-of-way permit issued by the director is subject to immediate revocation upon written notice if at any time the director determines that the use of the right-of-way authorized by the permit is inconsistent with or unreasonably impairs the public use of the right-of-way. The property owner is not required to comply with any right-of-way landscaping requirement if compliance is made impossible due to the director’s revocation of a right-of-way landscape permit.

(e) The issuance of a landscape permit under this section does not excuse the property owner, his agents, or employees from liability in the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, or pavement in the public right-of-way. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.125. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 26102)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-553.126. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 23929; 25163; 26102)
